content: I like to give descriptions and terrain features a lot while DMing. I like rping, character creation, going with the flow, and reward creativity above most else.  l enjoy social encounters with DCs and reskinning monsters. I enjoy helping people navigate situations that seem overwhelming and do well with newer players. I like creating small but useful magical items to be used creatively later when I've forgotten about them. I can run dark and scary sessions, unpack your trauma sessions, or silly whimsical wonder sessions. But ill fit whatever mood is set with direction.

I'm a chaotic good dm. I like world building and lore dumps. And shenanigans. I like to dm as though it is an improv play. I'm also a fair hand at game design. Above all I am here to tell stories, and sometimes rule following falls to the wayside, but I try my best to be fair. I love telling genre stories, and i pack everything with pop culture references.

I'm a little more rigid in my DM style, could be due to inexperience/lack of confidence, but this does make me fairly knowledgeable on rules of play.

I love crafting items. My favorite part of DnD is making magic items. The myriad of things that you can make...mmph.

My experience DMing is mostly one-shots, so a lot of my experience is a little wonky in that regard. That said, I really really like world-building and writing backstories. As you could probably tell from everything I put Web through, I like having characters go through hell (if that's what their player wants) and survive. I love using combat as a way to tell a story, with characters having to make decisions mid-fight that have impacts after the fighting is over. When I ask 'how do you want to do this?' that's not just an invitation to look cool. It's an invitation to tell me and the other players how your character thinks about what they're fighting and fighting in general. Do they try to non-lethal enemies or are they ruthless? Do they want to end things quickly or draw them out? Is your character even excited to be striking a killing blow? 
All this is to say that I really like telling stories. I'm full of rules knowledge so I can know exactly how they can be bent for the coolest moments.

Keep in mind this is my personal way I run my games, I am willing to change and do things differently for the sake of this game:

My style of DMing is very unorthodox. I rely heavily on my years of reading stories, watching movies, and playing games to be able to make a game up on the spot. I don't necessarily plan for one single game, instead I prefer to prepare for every type of game I possibly can. I let my players decide where they want to go and what they want to do.

Want to run a game in the sky and fight something? I know stats for airships and flying monsters by heart. Want to suddenly go underwater and explore? I already have 3 fully created underwater countries each with their own economy and system of government. I have every possible type of adventure someone might want to take in my head ready to be ran at a moment's notice. I also read every rule book cover to cover and dedicated every rule I could to memory. Though I tend to forget most of it and have to make something up on the spot 😛

However, even with all this preparation, I am willing to throw all of this out of the window for the sake of fun, and my players. For me, nothing matters more than making sure everyone is having fun, while also trying to some way make everything make some kind of logical sense. However the caveat is that everything will have consequences, whether that be good or bad. I am willing to let any and every character die. Especially if it's a result of their own choices. That being said, I will always give them a chance to survive. I'm not a jerk, I want their beloved characters to go on so they can keep having fun, but I do not pull punches, especially in combat.

Speaking of, I also run combat differently. Combat is another area where I can be mean in. Because I like keeping it moving, I have all the monster attacks already preplanned and sometimes even pre rolled. So when it comes to my players, if they do not have what they want to do ready, it is assumed they are taking the dodge action and skipped. I don't do it to be mean, but with how many players I tend to DM for, it slows things down to a crawl if they aren't ready. Oh, also if a player goes down, I don't let them roll death saves, I roll it for them secretly. I feel it gives people too much comfort to see their companion roll successes which discourages them from healing the downed party member. So I take that comfort away from them, which racks up the tension and encourages people to heal their downed companions.

To summarize, I am very nice and accommodating to nearly all of my players' requests. But I am mean when it comes to consequences and do not pull punches. However that being said, I know I make bad calls at times. So I give my players the chance to change what I did. If every player can agree that my call was wrong, and can agree what it should have been; I give up narrative control to them and let them change it. Because I recognize this is a group game, not "my" game. I am very flexible and willing to change anything and everything for the betterment of everyone else at the game.

So I feel you all already know the kind of DM I am, I am all about the story.  Regardless of murder hobos or role-players, I want people have a good story to tell when they get with their other nerd friends.  That doesn't mean every session is gold, but I make sure everyone gets their moment.  Likewise I love both Role playing and Roll playing.
I generally am more rules as written, since I teach new players a lot (one of my favorite things is to share this hobby with someone that has never played before) and I don't like teaching new players bad habits, or poor expectations of their next table.  Likewise, I set a few expectations when I sit at my table "This isn't me vs you, this is each player telling a story, and me making sure all the stories weave togeather."  Its my number 1 rule at my table.
Anyway, I love mechanics, homebrew, and balance.  My favorite is helping a person discover their character, both in character generation, as well as through the story.  In addition, helping someone create a backstory and character sheet is just gold to me.
All that said, where I lack most is time. I work two jobs, and have a non gaming wife.  So dedicating time to run combat is nearly impossible, but I often can roleplay or chat for long stretches while working.
If you have any questions about something, want to bounce and idea off someone, or really whatever, I am generally happy to discuss and help someone work through it, refine it, and make it as awesome as can be.

How do you feel about using "zones" for combat? I've always ran games either counting squares, or completely ignoring distance. In a theater-of-the-mind setting, squares doesn't work well, and completely ignoring distance slows down combat because players have ask about positions and relative distance. I was looking for better ways, to adjudicate, and found the zone thing. I've seen it in other games, but never D&D. It seems like it could work very well. It's assumed that you can move anywhere in your zone, move to an adjacent zone, and range attack into any zone. AoE attacks are a set number ahead of time. Has anyone run or played in games using zones? Any thoughts one way or the other?
Thats almost exactly how I ran all of season 3
You are either at melee or at range
Or out of range

The system I saw had zones like "throne room", "hallway", "Balcony". As you described the scene, you could specify who was where. Then you could go between them with a move action, double move to go two zones. Then an breath weapon would also only affect one zone. It seems to lend a bit more strategic utility than just everyone is within melee range of everyone, but still easy to run.
